title: Graded compatibility and isomorphism detection for already given filtered lifts
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. For $\mathcal C=\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, let $DF^+(\mathcal C)$ be the localization of bounded-below complexes with a finite decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] at maps inducing quasi-isomorphisms on all graded complexes. Write $\omega$ for forgetting the filtration and $DF^{+,[a,b]}(\mathcal C)$ for the full subcategory whose graded pieces vanish outside the integers $a\le p\le b$. Suppose exact functors $G_i:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ have already been equipped with exact filtered lifts $\widetilde G_i:DF^+(\mathcal A)\to DF^+(\mathcal B)$ preserving every interval $[a,b]$. Here an exact filtered lift means an exact functor with $\widetilde G_i(DF^{+,[a,b]}(\mathcal A))\subseteq DF^{+,[a,b]}(\mathcal B)$ together with a natural isomorphism $\phi_i:\omega\widetilde G_i\xrightarrow{\sim}G_i\omega$. Then there are canonical natural isomorphisms $\operatorname{gr}^p\widetilde G_i\xrightarrow{\sim}G_i\operatorname{gr}^p$ for every $p$. If a natural transformation $h:G_1\to G_2$ has already been supplied with a filtered lift, meaning a natural transformation $\widetilde h:\widetilde G_1\to\widetilde G_2$ satisfying $\phi_2\circ\omega\widetilde h=(h\omega)\circ\phi_1$, then these graded comparisons identify $\operatorname{gr}^p\widetilde h$ with $h\operatorname{gr}^p$. If $h$ is an isomorphism, $\widetilde h$ is an isomorphism. These comparisons are compatible with identity transformations, composition of already lifted transformations, and composition of filtered functors. This asserts properties of supplied lifts, not existence of a lift of an arbitrary ordinary natural transformation.
